title: Anya Taylor-Joy's Lucky Becomes Apple TV's Biggest Action Thriller of the Summer
excerpt: The seven-episode series, based on a bestselling novel and produced by Reese Witherspoon, reached No. 1 on the platform within 48 hours of its premiere.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Apple TV's Lucky became the platform's most-watched show within 48 hours of its July 15 premiere.
  • The seven-episode series holds an 81% critic score on Rotten Tomatoes, drawing heist film comparisons.
  • Lucky features a star-studded cast including Anya Taylor-Joy, Timothy Olyphant, and Annette Bening.
  • New episodes air weekly on Wednesdays through August 19, enhancing Apple TV's original programming lineup.

  • Apple TV's Lucky, starring Anya Taylor-Joy and Timothy Olyphant, became the platform's most-watched show within two days of its July 15 premiere
  • The seven-episode action thriller, based on Marissa Stapley's 2021 novel, holds an 81% critic score on Rotten Tomatoes and has drawn comparisons to classic heist films
  • Created by Jonathan Tropper and executive produced by Reese Witherspoon, Lucky features a star-studded cast including Annette Bening, Clifton Collins Jr., and Aunjanue Ellis-Taylor
  • New episodes air weekly on Wednesdays through August 19, with the show already helping Apple TV maintain its streak of high-profile original programming

Apple TV has another hit on its hands. Lucky, the action thriller starring Anya Taylor-Joy and Timothy Olyphant, reached the No. 1 spot on the streaming platform within 48 hours of its two-episode premiere on July 15, according to Apple TV's internal charts. The show has since been ranked among the most-watched series in the United States across all streaming platforms.

The series follows Luciana "Lucky" Armstrong, a con artist played by Taylor-Joy, whose latest heist in Las Vegas goes catastrophically wrong. With the FBI, a dangerous crime boss, and her own past closing in on her, Lucky must navigate a high-stakes chase across the American Southwest — all while piecing together what happened to her missing partner, Cary, played by Drew Starkey.

A Star-Studded Cast Anchors the Thriller

Taylor-Joy, fresh off her action turn in Apple TV's The Gorge, brings a sharp physicality and emotional range to the role. Timothy Olyphant, the Emmy-nominated star of Justified and Apple TV's Stick, plays Lucky's father John Armstrong — a career criminal whose complicated relationship with his daughter sits at the heart of the narrative.

Annette Bening rounds out the central triangle as Priscilla Masterson, Cary's mother and a seasoned criminal who is hunting Lucky for her own reasons. Clifton Collins Jr. plays Priscilla's enforcer Harris Dutch, while Aunjanue Ellis-Taylor stars as FBI Agent Billie Rand, leading the federal investigation into Lucky and Cary's multimillion-dollar heist.

"The show maintains its dynamism because it remains character-driven."

— Variety

From Bestseller to Streaming Hit

The series is adapted from Marissa Stapley's 2021 novel Lucky, a Reese's Book Club pick that December. Witherspoon serves as executive producer through her production company Hello Sunshine, alongside creator Jonathan Tropper, who previously helmed Apple TV's dark comedy Your Friends & Neighbors.

Notably, the adaptation drops the novel's lottery ticket subplot — in the book, Lucky wins a lottery jackpot and must find a way to claim the money while on the run — in favor of a tighter focus on the pursuit itself. The cat-and-mouse structure, intercut with flashbacks exploring Lucky's upbringing, has drawn comparisons to classic heist thrillers.

The show holds an 81% critic score on Rotten Tomatoes. CBR's review praised Taylor-Joy and Bening as "the saving graces of the show," while noting the series could have spent more time on the emotional stakes between Lucky and her father rather than Lucky and her husband.

Apple TV's Growing Dominance in Premium Television

Lucky's debut continues what has been a strong run for Apple TV in 2026. The platform's sci-fi flagship Silo recently broke records with 500 days at the No. 1 spot. Cape Fear, the Javier Bardem–led psychological thriller that premiered in early June, has been a consistent top-three performer throughout its first season. And Ted Lasso returns for a fourth season on August 5.

For Taylor-Joy, the role further cements her status as one of Hollywood's most versatile performers. She will next appear in Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part Three, reprising her role as Alia Atreides. Olyphant, meanwhile, has Netflix's The Adventures of Cliff Booth and a second season of Stick on the horizon.

What Indian Audiences Should Know

Apple TV's subscriber base in India has grown significantly since 2024, and the platform's action thrillers have consistently performed well in Indian markets. Lucky is available globally on Apple TV, with new episodes releasing every Wednesday through August 19 for a total of seven episodes.
